hourly.summary: Manchester United fans are in full meltdown after Lisandro Martinez publicly torched the club's transfer policy and hierarchy post-Atletico defeat, sparking a civil war between the dressing room and the 'laptop class' at Carrington. With the worst start in 40 years, the Amazon documentary crew capturing the car crash in 4K, and INEOS's honeymoon officially over, the fanbase has united behind a centre-back saying what they've all been screaming into the void for years.

daily.summary: The day began with pre-match dread and gallows humor as fans braced for a Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid, but the 2-0 loss triggered a full-blown meltdown — Lisandro Martinez's explosive post-match takedown of the hierarchy, a fifth straight winless game, and open talk of protests crystallized the worst start in 40 years into an existential crisis.

weekly.summary: The week began with fragile optimism during the international break but rapidly deteriorated after a shocking opening-day loss to Hull City, triggering a sustained downward spiral. A brief moment of cautious stability mid-week evaporated as a worsening injury crisis and a disastrous 1-1 home draw against 10-man Tottenham extended United's worst start in 40 years, culminating in open revolt with 'Carrick Out' chants and total loss of faith in the project. The dominant arc is a collapse from uneasy hope into full-blown crisis, with only academy graduates providing any respite from the gloom.
